title: Cato De Agri Cultura 133 attached layering and basket transplant constructor
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED. Cato 133 gives a complete cultivation mechanism in which a scion remains attached while rooting, then is cut and transplanted; an on-tree perforated basket branch preserves attachment, age, root state, cut boundary, and container through planting. This is distinct from seed extraction and graft compatibility.

source.source_span: complete layering, on-tree basket, and vine timing instructions; accessed page lines 32-34
source.source_limit: public-domain Loeb translation page; no claim about a target Vorlage or modern horticultural efficacy

steps: ATTACH scion to parent; PRESS_INTO_SOIL while TIP remains outside
DIG at proper time and TRANSPLANT_VERTICAL as a planted individual
For careful propagation THREAD shoot through perforated container, PACK with earth, and LEAVE_ATTACHED on tree
At the source's age branch CUT_BELOW and PLANT_WITH_CONTAINER; vine branch changes waiting age only

consequence: The same propagule has states ATTACHED_AND_ROOTING then DETACHED_AND_PLANTED; parent remains a separate participant and the basket can persist into planting.

rivals.R-CUT: Detach first and root later; predicts no on-tree waiting state or persistent parent relation.
rivals.R-GRAFT: Fuse donor and stock; predicts merged identity rather than a rooted shoot retaining its container.

missing_target_binding: No target word is assigned to parent, scion, attachment, root, age, cut, container, orientation, or planting.
likely_failure: If a future target lacks globally reusable attachment/root/age/cut/container relations, the constructor cannot discriminate its rivals and remains raw.
